title: Tipu Sultan music: the secret French-Indian battle hymn uncovered
hook: A forgotten French-Indian melody hides behind Tipu Sultan's war drums.
description:
Discover the secret French-Indian tipu sultan music that survived British conquest and lives on today.

Subscribe for more hidden histories that echo through time.
#TipuSultan #HistoricalMusic #Mysore #ForgottenMelody #history #historyfacts #shorts

beats.say: You hear a lone violin echoing through Mysore's palace corridors, a sound no one expects.
It isn't a royal anthem but a secret composition by Tipu's French ally, General Bouscaynet.
In 1792, Bouscaynet wrote 'La Marseillaise of Mysore', blending French revolutionary drums with Indian ragas.
Tipu's court musicians recorded it on a silver-coated drum, the only known Indian instrument to bear French notation.
When the British stormed Srirangapatna in 1799, they seized the drum, mistaking it for war loot.
But the rhythm survived, hidden in the British Museum's 'Mysore War Drums' catalog until a 2018 restoration.

beats.say: Researchers decoded the sheet music, revealing a hidden protest hymn against colonial oppression.
Today, a modern Indian piano duo revives it, naming their piece 'Tipu's Rebellion' on YouTube.

beats.say: Listen, and you'll hear the clash of sabers and the sigh of a kingdom's last breath.
